newsitem.title: UK: Sept Forties cargoes delayed by Nelson maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Sept Forties cargoes delayed by Nelson maintenance.

text.p: All Forties cargoes scheduled for the second half of September will load a day later than planned due to lower than expected production from Britain's biggest crude oil stream, trading sources said on Thursday.
"All the cargoes loading in the second half of the month have been delayed by one day," said an equity holder.
Trading sources said the delays were caused by Enterprise Oil's decision to bring forward by six months planned maintenance at its Nelson field.
"Originally the shutdown was planned for next March but there were a couple of jobs which couldn't wait until then so we decided to do it in September," an Enterprise official told Reuters.
Nelson, which usually pumps about 160,000 barrels per day (bpd), will be closed from September 12 to September 24.
Traders said a couple of smaller fields in the system were producing at a lower than expected rate but no September cargoes have been cancelled.
"Forties is such a tight system that underperformance at one field can quickly cause problems," said an equity producer.
Market talk suggesting Amerada Hess' Scott field was experiencing difficulties was strenously denied by an equity producer.
"Scott is doing fine, there is no problem with the field," he said.
Reduced output from Nelson and Scott earlier this year forced Forties operator British Petroleum Co Plc (BP) to delay March loading dates.
The original September Forties loading programme scheduled the equivalent of 46.2 standard 500,000-barrel cargoes, including the equivalent of three shipments direct to BP's Grangemouth refinery.

September volumes were expected to total 23.1 million barrels, according to the programme, made up of 16 cargoes of 600,000 barrels, 24 of 500,000 barrels and 1.5 million barrels to Forties system operator BP's refinery.
Forties cargoes are loaded from the Hound Point terminal in eastern Scotland.
